pack.subject: molecular-biology
pack.title: Telomeres and telomerase
pack.summary: How cells copy and protect the ends of their chromosomes.

concepts.name: Telomeres
concepts.summary: Repeated DNA at chromosome ends that protects them from loss and fusion.

concepts.name: Telomerase
concepts.summary: The enzyme that extends telomeres using its own RNA template.

items.explanation: Telomeres are tandem repeats of a short DNA sequence; proteins bind them, but they aren't proteins.

items.prompt: Why do telomeres shorten with each round of replication in most somatic cells?
choices: The lagging strand can't be finished at the very end
DNA polymerase cuts them off on purpose
items.explanation: The last primer on the lagging strand leaves a gap that polymerase can't fill, so the end shortens.

items.prompt: Put these in the order they happen as a cell line keeps dividing without telomerase.
items.explanation: Shortening comes first; at a critical length the ends look like damage, which stops division.

items.prompt: Which molecule serves as telomerase's template?
items.explanation: Telomerase is a reverse transcriptase that carries its own RNA template.

items.prompt: A tumour's cells keep dividing for decades. What would you most expect in them?
items.explanation: Most cancers reactivate telomerase, which keeps telomeres long enough to keep dividing.
